Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the InnovaTech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Lewis, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Lewis, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to InnovaTech’s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Mark Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Lee, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Mark.

Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

We made strong progress this quarter. Our Q4 2023 wafer sales performance demonstrates a solid end to the year, marked by a significant increase in shipment volume and a stabilization of Average Selling Prices (ASPs) across key segments. As previously stated, wafer shipment volume rose to 2.3 million 8-inch equivalent units in Q4. This represents a 7% increase compared to Q3 2023 and a 3% increase compared to Q4 2022, signaling a continued, albeit moderate, recovery in demand across several core application areas.

We also saw great momentum in the automotive segment. Overall, Q3 2024 demonstrates a positive trajectory for the company, driven primarily by a strong rebound in the automotive sector and strategic allocation of resources to alleviate global chip shortages impacting that critical market. While other segments show moderate growth, the automotive segment significantly outperformed expectations. We are seeing margin improvements across all segments, attributable to operational efficiencies and strategic pricing adjustments.

These achievements underscore our commitment to disciplined execution and innovation.

Now I’ll pass it to Sarah to walk through in more detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mark, and hello, everyone.

Let me take you through the financials:

First, building on what Mark said, we’ve continued to drive improvements there, specifically in the automotive segment. Automotive Q3 revenue was $2.3 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth is significantly higher than our initial projections of 8%, demonstrating the effectiveness of our resource prioritization strategy focused on the automotive market.

We invested strategically in this area, resulting in gross margin reaching 23.9%, translating to TWD 10.8 billion. This represents a solid performance for the quarter, driven by several key factors. Firstly, a favorable product mix shift towards higher-margin enterprise solutions in the APAC region contributed approximately 1.5 percentage points to the gross margin. Specifically, the increased adoption of our cloud-based security suite by large financial institutions in Singapore and Hong Kong, which carry significantly higher margins than our legacy on-premise software, played a crucial role. Secondly, successful implementation of our "Project Phoenix" supply chain optimization initiative, aimed at streamlining component sourcing and manufacturing processes, resulted in a reduction in direct material costs, adding another 0.8 percentage points to the gross margin. Finally, a slight weakening of the TWD against the USD during the quarter provided a modest tailwind, accounting for approximately 0.2 percentage points.

Additionally, we’ve seen progress in government subsidies and tax incentives. Our financial projections for the period 2021-2023 are heavily reliant on the continued availability and recognition of government subsidies, local grants, and favorable tax incentives. As highlighted in previous reports, these financial instruments play a crucial role in supporting our operational efficiency, capital expenditure programs, and research & development initiatives, and we believe we are well-positioned to continue to leverage these opportunities.

Now I’ll turn it over to David, who will speak about operations and innovation.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

Let me begin with a closer look at wafer sales and the breakdown to wafer quantity and ASP for this quarter, particularly on shipment volume. Shipments of 8-inch wafers accounted for approximately 1.5 million units, representing 65% of the total volume. This segment saw a 5% sequential increase from Q3, driven primarily by demand from the analog and power management IC sectors. Specifically, the automotive industry's continued reliance on mature node technologies for power management, as well as increased adoption of IoT devices requiring cost-effective solutions, fueled this growth. We anticipate continued strong demand for 8-inch wafers in these sectors moving into 2024, albeit at a potentially decelerated rate as new fab capacities come online globally. The remaining 0.8 million units consisted of 12-inch wafers, accounting for 35% of total shipments. This segment experienced a more robust 10% sequential increase, reflecting the growing demand for advanced node technologies used in high-performance computing (HPC), AI, and mobile applications. A significant portion of this growth can be attributed to our strategic partnership with QuantumLeap Technologies, a leading AI chip designer, who ramped up production volumes for their new GPU architecture in Q4. We also saw a noticeable uptick in demand from memory manufacturers, particularly for DRAM used in data centers. We introduced the WaferTrace initiative, and it’s already contributing to justifying our pricing.

I’d also like to expand on Q1 2024 sales guidance. Our Q1 2024 sales guidance reflects a cautiously optimistic outlook, driven primarily by anticipated incremental improvements in wafer shipment volumes. As the summary indicates, we project a slight increase in wafer shipments compared to Q4 2023, stemming largely from higher utilization rates across our existing fabrication facilities. We are forecasting this increase to translate to modest revenue growth across several key segments, though macroeconomic uncertainties continue to present headwinds. Our teams have made solid progress here, projecting an overall wafer shipment increase of approximately 3-5% quarter-over-quarter for Q1 2024. This translates to an estimated shipment volume of 1.15 million to 1.17 million wafers (equivalent 12-inch) compared to the 1.12 million wafers shipped in Q4 2023. This increase is contingent upon maintaining and further optimizing our current operational efficiencies. We are targeting a 92% average utilization rate across our global fabrication network, a 2-percentage point improvement from Q4 2023’s average of 90%.

Let’s move to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
You mentioned strong improvements in the automotive segment. Can you talk more about the key trends you're observing within that segment?

Sarah Chen:
Certainly. We're seeing a few key trends driving growth in the automotive sector. Electric Vehicle (EV) penetration is a major factor. Demand for our EV-related chipsets increased by 28% year-over-year, driven by the accelerating adoption of electric vehicles globally. This is a key growth area for the automotive segment. Also, ADAS Integration is becoming more prevalent. We witnessed a significant uptick in demand for our ADAS solutions, particularly Level 2 and Level 3 systems. Automakers are increasingly integrating these features into their vehicles to enhance safety and driving experience.

Analyst 2:
Can you elaborate on the trajectory of government subsidies and tax incentives and the specific impact of the ITC?

David Lee:
Sure. In 2020, we received approximately $75 million in government grants across various programs. We anticipate a similar level of funding in 2021, holding steady at around $72-78 million. We estimate that the ITC contributed approximately $18 million to our bottom line in 2020 and expect a similar impact in 2021, assuming no significant changes to the ITC policy. Specifically, in Q3 2021, we anticipate receiving a tax refund of approximately $4.5 million, related to unused ITC credits from prior years. Furthermore, in the last quarter, we are expecting a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. The federal tax incentives are essential to our growth.

Analyst 3:
With regard to gross margin results, how does Q4 2020 compare to your guidance from the Q3 2020 earnings call?

Sarah Chen:
During our Q3 2020 earnings call, we guided for a Q4 2020 gross margin in the range of 24.0% to 24.5%. Our actual Q4 2020 gross margin of 23.9% falls slightly below the lower end of this range. This deviation is primarily due to the following: The global supply chain disruptions proved more severe than initially projected in Q3, resulting in higher-than-anticipated shipping and logistics costs. We had initially factored in a moderate increase in these costs, but the actual increase exceeded our expectations, impacting gross margins by approximately 0.3 percentage points. Also, a sudden surge in demand for certain semiconductor components, particularly microcontrollers, resulted in component shortages and increased procurement costs. This unforeseen event impacted our ability to fully optimize our bill of materials and negatively impacted gross margins by approximately 0.2 percentage points.

Closing

Mark Thompson:
Thank you all for joining us today. We're energized by the momentum we’re seeing and look forward to sharing continued progress next quarter.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
